_comment: Phase 71 example article — TRANSLUCENTTHICK. The defining observable is ABSORPTION WITH DEPTH: the colour deepens through the body, and the high IOR bends what you see through it. Param-only (no maps — a gemstone has no albedo texture). `thin_walled: false` is THE OpenPBR discriminator that makes this Thick and not Thin. Routes by the `diamond` leaf-stem name exception (class mineral -> Opaque otherwise). ** transmission is 1.0 -- the PHYSICALLY CORRECT value, and it is safe again. History (71.12): the master computed `opacity = Opacity * (1 - Transmission)`, so an honest 1.0 drove opacity to ZERO -- the body vanished and the gem rendered as a view-dependent Fresnel mirror ('clear mirror at some angles, clear plane at others'), roughness inert because no lit body remained. The stopgap was to fudge this to 0.95 (as 71.11 had already been forced to do to Glass). That was treating the symptom: it meant every fully-transmissive article had to UNDER-STATE its own physics to survive the master. The master now FLOORS the opacity (MIN_TRANSMISSIVE_OPACITY, bake_master_authortier.py), so an article never has to lie -- and this is restored to 1.0. **
name: Diamond_Brilliant_Clean_Base_s01_v01
